name: epoll_pwait2
synopsis: int epoll_wait(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, int timeout);
int epoll_pwait(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, int timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable sigmask);
int epoll_pwait2(int epfd, struct epoll_event *events, int maxevents, const struct timespec *_Nullable timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable sigmask);
description: epoll_pwait2 waits for I/O events on an epoll file descriptor, allowing specification of a timeout using a timespec structure and a signal mask to block signals during the wait. It is similar to epoll_pwait but provides more precise timeout handling.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: Pointer to a buffer to store the events

parameters.name: maxevents
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to return

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Pointer to a timespec structure for the timeout, or NULL for indefinite

parameters.name: sigmask
parameters.description: Pointer to a signal set to block signals, or NULL

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors ready for I/O, or zero if the timeout expires
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: epfd is not a valid file descriptor
The memory area pointed to by events is not accessible with write permissions
The call was interrupted by a signal handler before events occurred or timeout expired
epfd is not an epoll file descriptor, or maxevents is less than or equal to zero

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.37, a timeout value larger than approximately LONG_MAX / HZ milliseconds is treated as -1 (infinite).
